about: Katherine is one of the daughters of Nick and Yolyn Goldschmidt, a New Zealand winemaking family based in Healdsburg since 1990, and one of three sisters who have become winemakers under their father’s guidance. Nick ran the cellar at Simi in the 1990s and later led winemaking for Allied Domecq and Beam Estates; his own label sticks to single vineyards and single varieties, and this Cabernet is the family’s approachable Alexander Valley bottling.

Stonemason Hill is a hillside vineyard at about 500 feet, planted in 1989 with the Jackson clone of Cabernet on sandy Bale loam and cane-pruned on vertical trellises. The 2023 season was cool and wet, delaying budbreak and stretching harvest into autumn, so the grapes ripened slowly and kept their acidity. The wine is 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, aged in medium-toast French oak of which only 15% is new, and left unfined, which makes it vegan.

The winemaker notes cherry and blueberry with a little French vanilla from the oak; Wine Enthusiast adds raspberry coulis, black plum, fresh herbs and dark chocolate, with fine tannins, bright acidity and a long, plush finish. James Suckling calls it creamy and soft, ready to drink now, while the producer suggests it will keep through about 2035.
